articles.title: Trump told European leaders they were spending a lot on Ukraine, Zelensky says
articles.summary: KYIV, Nov 21 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump told European leaders this week they were spending a lot on the war in Ukraine and could use that money at home if a peace deal were reached with Russia, Ukrainian President ‌Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Saturday. Trump called into a meeting of Ukraine's Coalition of the Willing allies in Berlin on Thursday following ‌his trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at an APEC summit in Shenzhen. "He said that Europe is spending a lot of money, and they ​could spend it on themselves after the end (of the war)," Zelenskiy, who attended the meeting in Berlin, told reporters before talks with British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv. "It didn't sound like a threat." Trump said on his return to Washington on Friday that Putin had clearly expressed his desire to end the war in Ukraine by  diplomatic means during their talks. But Zelenskiy said he was not convinced about Putin's intentions. "I'm a little bit more skeptical than ‌Americans that he's ready for compromises. That's what ⁠I said to the American team, by the way," he said. Putin has shown no sign of dropping his demand that Ukraine surrender all of its eastern region of Donbas in return for peace. Zelenskiy has rejected this, saying ⁠many Ukrainian soldiers have died defending land there since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Zelenskiy welcomed recent announcements by US envoys on including Europe as full partners in the peace process, which resumed after a nine-month hiatus with talks in Abu Dhabi this month. But he said the US envoys now needed to agree ​an ​agenda and the timing for another round of talks. "Certainly, America will try to ​make the meeting happen as soon as possible. And I ‌am confident Russia will take all steps to slightly postpone such a meeting," Zelenskiy said. Putin accused Kyiv and Europe on Thursday of not being able to make compromises to resolve the war in Ukraine. STREETING VISIT Zelenskiy reiterated on Saturday that he was ready to attend a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which Trump is due to host next month in Miami, and that he would be happy to hold direct talks with Putin there. So far he has not been invited. Zelenskiy said Streeting's visit, following a heavy Russian bombardment of Kyiv this week, was an important ‌show of solidarity. Putin had promised retaliation for airstrikes that crippled a major bridge ​linking Crimea, which Russia seized and annexed in 2014, to Russia's Krasnodar region this week. Zelenskiy ​dismissed Putin's assertion that the bridge had been used only ​for civilian transportation, saying a search of social media showed hundreds of images of military vehicles crossing the bridge. Zelenskiy ‌said Russia had again attacked civilian targets overnight in the ​industrial city of Kryvyi Rih - his ​hometown - where at least two people were killed, including a seven-year-old boy. Both sides denied deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. Streeting said it was pointless for Putin to use the language of peace at international summits if his forces then bombarded civilian infrastructure. Streeting said a Russian ​violation of Polish airspace - which Polish authorities said ‌was probably by two missiles and a drone - before military exercises on Friday for the "Coalition of the Willing" was "an outrageous provocation". "The ​best response, and the response that I would appeal to all of our allies to undertake, is to do more ​to support Ukraine," he said. (Reporting by Daniel Flynn, Editing by Timothy Heritage) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/trump-told-european-leaders-were-145057566.html

articles.title: FBI's most-wanted cartel kingpin captured as gunfire erupts across Mexican city
articles.summary: Watch as Cartel kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list is arrested in Mexico - Clipped From Video Mexico’s military captured an alleged drug lord listed among the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, sparking violent exchanges of gunfire in Sinaloa state on Friday that sent fans fleeing from a baseball game. Mexico’s defense ministry said Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” who leads the Sinaloa-based cartel Los Mazatlecos, was arrested with the help of the US. CNN has approached US authorities for comment. The operation was conducted by “elite military forces” using “stealth and surprise” to reach their target, the ministry posted on X, saying Meza-Flores was taken to Mexico City following his arrest. Two other alleged members of the criminal organization were arrested in the same operation, Mexico’s Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said in a post on X . They include the group’s second-in-command, Germán “N,” alias “Serafín,” and José “N,” its alleged financial operator. Meza-Flores is “allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution, and importation of large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States,” according to an FBI wanted poster offering a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. He was previously indicted in 2019 for drug trafficking violations and possession of a firearm, and in 2012 for drug trafficking charges, it said. Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores. - US Department of State In a 2013 statement, the US Treasury Department said the Meza-Flores cartel had been involved in “an extremely violent turf war” with the rival Sinaloa Cartel – then led by notorious drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, who is now serving time in a US prison. The operation to capture Meza-Flores sparked violent clashes on Friday between the Mexican military and armed militants in Guasave, an area known as the agricultural heart of Mexico. The defense ministry said that authorities “came under attack with gunfire and explosives” upon initiating the operation, and that militants set up roadblocks in several municipalities near the arrest site. Dramatic footage, verified by CNN, shows a barrage of rapid fire from what appear to be Mexican security force helicopters firing at the ground and circling over Guasave city. Local authorities confirmed “an attack on federal personnel” in the city. Baseball fans at the Kuroda Park stadium scrambled out of the stands as a barrage of gunfire rang out on Friday night local time, in footage geolocated by CNN. “Get down, duck down, down, down!” one person shouted in the panic as people clambered over barriers and a baby was heard crying off-camera. An official broadcast showed players from Venados de Mazatlán and Algodoneros de Guasave teams fleeing the field mid-game. “It’s being suspended… there’s a situation happening off the field,” the announcers inform viewers on the broadcast . “We wish first and foremost to ask God that everything is OK… there is a national security incident, it may be better for us to go to break now.” The game, part of the 2026 Liga Mexicana – the country’s premier summer professional baseball league – began at 9:30 p.m. EST. A local resident, running errands when the violence erupted, said private hospitals had been taken over by armed individuals, and businesses including convenience stores and gas stations were being set on fire. “I had to take shelter inside some shops that pulled down their security shutters well before closing time,” he told CNN, speaking on condition of anonymity. “People are still trapped inside. “Just meters away from where I was, a convoy of heavily armed civilians passed by, firing shots.” Sinaloa’s state government urged Guasave residents to stay indoors and avoid traveling on the roads, in a statement late Friday. unknown content item - “Authorities from the Interagency Group have been deployed in an operation to restore order, which will be reported once the security operation concludes,” it added. CNN has contacted a representative for the Mexican federal government, Liga Mexicana, Kuroda Park, and both baseball teams playing at the stadium Friday night for comment. articles.title: Jan. 6 leader who once backed Trump now says he's 'absolutely done'
articles.summary: IRVING, Texas (AP) — Stewart Rhodes didn’t just go to prison for Donald Trump . While serving time for his role in the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, the founder of the right-wing militia known as the Oath Keepers got a tattoo of Trump’s defiant face after he survived an assassin’s bullet in Butler, Pennsylvania . It was further proof of Rhodes' devotion to the Republican president. But that's all over now. “I am absolutely done with Trump,” said Rhodes, sitting at a rickety yellow table outside a gastropub in Irving, Texas. He considers Trump not just a traitor, but "one of the very worst in our nation's history.” The repudiation from a former acolyte — one convicted of seditious conspiracy for orchestrating an ill-fated attempt to keep Trump in power six years ago — is another example of how allegiance to the president has faded even among extreme supporters. Back then, Rhodes claimed Trump lost the 2020 White House race to Democrat Joe Biden because of election fraud. This year in Texas, where Democrats had historic victories , he said there's another reason. “The lion’s share is because Trump pissed off his own base," Rhodes said, his face shaded by a black cowboy hat. An eye patch covers his left socket, the result of an old gun accident, and a glacial blue iris peers out from the other. Nearby, people mingled with drinks for his Christian Warriors After-Party, organized during a three-day conference called “Christ is King: America After Trump.” Some people approached to shake hands or sign up for the Oath Keepers or trainings for things like community defense and hurricane relief. ‘The first inkling’ of a split from Trump The beginning of Rhodes' break with Trump came when the president gave pardons to hundreds of people who were locked up for their actions on Jan. 6, 2021, but only commuted Rhodes' sentence . “That was the first inkling,” Rhodes said. Rhodes also said Trump's war with Iran violated Trump's promises to end foreign conflicts. And, Rhodes said, it felt like an affront when Trump dismissed people who urged his administration to release files about the Jeffrey Epstein case , calling them “PAST supporters.” Then Rhodes felt Trump went back on his longtime slogan. “We elected him to end the corruption in Washington, D.C. ‘Drain the swamp.’ Unfortunately his administration has been one of the most corrupt administrations in U.S. history," Rhodes said. “The pardons are pay-for-play and everything is pay-for-play.” The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Rhodes is not alone in his about-face on Trump, but there's an ideological through line, said Sam Jackson, an associate professor at the University at Albany with a focus on anti-government extremism. “They went from seeing Donald Trump as their ally in this fight against the conspiracy, to actually being co-opted by the conspiracy,” Jackson said, and it “points to deeper consistency in that understanding of the world as driven by hidden, evil actors.” Rhodes, who graduated from Yale Law School and worked for former U.S. Rep. Ron Paul of Texas, founded the Oath Keepers in 2009 with the goal of encouraging members of the military and law enforcement to resist what they view as unconstitutional orders, such as disarming citizens or carrying out warrantless searches. Watching from prison when Trump was fired on Rhodes later allied himself with Trump's political movement, and the Oath Keepers supported his attempt to remain in office after losing the 2020 election. Fueled with conspiracies about voter fraud, prosecutors said group members gathered weapons, organized trainings and assembled in Washington , where some helped storm the Capitol on Jan. 6. Rhodes, who did not enter the building that day, said he was a “political prisoner" who faced “illegality” in his trial. He was sentenced to 18 years, one of the longest sentences of any Jan. 6 case. “You are smart, you are charismatic and compelling and frankly that’s what makes you dangerous,” U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta said during the hearing. “The moment you are released, whenever that may be, you will be ready to take up arms against your government.” Rhodes was behind bars as Trump began his political comeback. He said he watched the assassination attempt in Butler on a prison television with other inmates. He saw Trump pump his fist and yell “fight,” and he figured that God’s hand was on the man. After Trump won the 2024 election, he swiftly pardoned hundreds of people convicted of crimes related to Jan. 6, including those who assaulted police officers. Rhodes received a commutation, which didn’t wipe his record clean. “He let us out of prison. We were grateful. I didn’t get a pardon though,” he said. Tattoo that honored Trump will be ‘modified’ to reflect a new reality The Justice Department vacated Rhodes' conviction earlier this year, lifting his felon status. Rhodes said he's working to rebuild the Oath Keepers, which previously had tens of thousands of members, according to leaked lists. With his rights restored, Rhodes said his first priority was to get some guns, and he didn't register to vote in time for the election. But he said he wouldn't have cast a ballot anyway. That's because Rhodes felt that “the Republican Party has taken us for granted," and he didn't want to choose between “a half a dose of poison or a full dose.” As for his tattoo of Trump, the man he now considers a traitor, Rhodes has plans that he didn't specify. “I will have this prison tattoo of Trump ‘modified,'” he wrote in a text message, “to reflect that reality. That treason.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/oath-keepers-founder-jan-6-130043975.html

articles.title: More trouble for Nvidia as SEC reportedly probes accounting amid historic stock slide
articles.summary: Nvidia's worst week on record just got worse. Now the government is asking questions about its books. Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock fell 14% Friday, its worst day since the DeepSeek rout in January 2025 and its seventh straight loss, before bouncing nearly 4% in after-hours trading. The drop came as Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission's probe of the chipmaker is examining potential accounting issues. The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that the probe includes an examination of whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. Nvidia didn't respond to Bloomberg's request for comment on that report, and the SEC declined to comment. The selling set records. Nvidia shed about $490 billion in market value Friday and nearly $900 billion this week, as its stock had its worst week since October 2008. That tops the $573 billion it lost last week, previously the biggest one-week drop for any company on record, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Since its Oct. 6 record, Nvidia has lost about $2.7 trillion in market value, more than the $2.5 trillion that The Kobeissi Letter called the biggest 45-day loss for any stock in history. The world's most valuable company six weeks ago now ranks fourth in the US, behind Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ). Nvidia's latest quarterly report raised a few questions. The company said its 10-Q, the detailed quarterly filing, would come "in the coming weeks" instead of the same evening as usual, and the release mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee. Nvidia booked about $104 billion of revenue through its Singapore unit in 2025, roughly half its sales, the Financial Times reported. The Journal said the disclosure questions include Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer US officials suspect of rerouting its chips to China. Nvidia's customers are also taking longer to pay, with bills outstanding at 64 days of sales, the most since 2022. It's not clear which of these, if any, the SEC is focused on. Washington wants answers fast. "I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's exit as CEO. President Trump said Friday he "would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," while criticizing the chipmaker's new leadership . California is digging in too. Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia Thursday, investigating whether its advanced chips reached China and whether the company misled investors. "Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said. The sell-off spread across chip stocks , which had their worst week since 2001 , and the broader market. Baird's Ted Mortonson, a technology desk sector strategist, saw more scrutiny coming even before Friday's report. "Every single deal that Nvidia has done on circular finance is going to be put under the microscope," he said on Yahoo Finance's live show Thursday. articles.title: Jensen Huang's next move: Wall Street floats Intel and SpaceX
articles.summary: F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote that there are no second acts in American lives. Silicon Valley has spent 40 years proving him wrong. Jensen Huang has been out as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO for barely a week, and everyone already has a script for him. President Donald Trump, who has defended Huang from the start, would prefer a rerun. "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump said at a White House briefing Friday , adding that a smart Nvidia would accept Huang's apology and let him return. The casting call comes in one of the worst weeks for tech stocks in years. Nvidia has lost more than $2.7 trillion in market value since its Oct. 6 record high, nearly $900 billion of it this week, as an SEC probe reportedly looks into its accounting. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) closed in a correction Friday, and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) lost 10% for the week. Wall Street has its own scripts. Speculation from Mizuho cites Huang as leading Intel's ( INTC ) AI chip strategy, though no talks have been reported. Asked on X about hiring Huang, Elon Musk replied , "That would be an honor." Musk has also said he's signing a petition to reinstate Huang at Nvidia, along with Uber founder Travis Kalanick, who staged a second act of his own after Uber pushed him out in 2017. The people putting money on it are backing neither. On Polymarket , the top pick for Huang's next formal role is a company he starts himself, at 27%, ahead of no new job before 2028, at 24%. A return to Nvidia gets 20%, SpaceX 8%, and Intel 3%, in a small market with about $64,000 traded. Apple bought NeXT 11 years after that, and Jobs came with it. Musk was pushed out as PayPal's CEO in 2000 and founded SpaceX ( SPCX ) about 18 months later, so the company floated for Huang is itself a second act. Intel would cast Huang as Lee Iacocca. Henry Ford II fired Iacocca as president of Ford ( F ) in 1978, and within four months, he was running the struggling Chrysler, which was later rescued by federal loan guarantees. Washington has owned roughly 10% of Intel since August 2025. But Huang is still Nvidia's largest individual shareholder, with a stake worth about $102 billion at Friday's close. articles.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks have increased to highest level since Iran war began
articles.summary: Reported attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz have been higher in number in October and November than any previous months since the war between the U.S., Israel and Iran began in late February , according to data compiled by maritime organizations. The attacks appear to be a bid to complicate U.S.-led efforts to keep oil flowing through the economically crucial Strait of Hormuz despite an Iranian-declared blockade, experts told ABC News. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) reported 31 attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October, and about 19 in November, as of Nov. 18. Noppadon Wongsuvan via AP Photo - PHOTO: Smoke billows from the Mayuree Naree, a Thailand-flagged bulk carrier, after it was hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, north of Oman, on March 11, 2026. Previously, a total of 53 incidents had been reported to the UKMTO between March and September of this year, averaging 10 to 15 incidents total across both Strait of Hormuz and surrounding gulfs in previous months. The International Maritime Organization (IMO), a United Nations agency, has slightly more conservative numbers, with 34 attacks confirmed in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October and November so far. This too, is still a marked increase from previous numbers the IMO had collected, which number roughly 50 in and around the Strait of Hormuz between March and September. The IMO has tallied 138 attacks on vessels in total across the Middle East since the war began. The positions of attacked tankers reported to the UKMTO indicate that most attacked vessels were in the very southern portion of the Strait of Hormuz, staying close to the Omani coastline, according to the maritime group's data. Social media via Reuters - PHOTO: Smoke rises at sea off the coast of Oman, Nov. 18, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a social media video. What experts say Iran aims to accomplish "Iran's objective remains to keep the Omani route, which is described as a U.S.-facilitated route, a very high-risk passage and to keep the energy recovery inconsistent," Noam Raydan, senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, told ABC News. Felt Maps/UKMTO/Verified UGC  - PHOTO: Map identifying locations where vessels were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz in October and November of 2026, according to UKMTO data. "Washington and its regional partners have found ways to keep oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz," Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group (ICG) think tank, told ABC News. "Tehran now seems determined to make these arrangements more costly and less reliable." The workaround developed by the U.S. involves "ship-to-ship" (STS) transfers in which smaller tankers cross the strait with tracking systems switched off, and transfer cargos to larger tankers once safely on the other side, Sina Toossi, senior fellow with the Center for International Policy, told ABC News. Iran is now responding in "a cycle of adaptation and counter-adaptation," he said. "Tehran has escalated its attacks to make the STS system more dangerous, costly, and ultimately unviable. Iran's broader objective is to demonstrate that normal oil exports cannot continue while the US maintains its blockade of Iran, and to generate enough economic pressure to force Washington to negotiate an end to the conflict," Toossi said. The U.S. has maintained a naval blockade, stopping Iranian and Iran-linked ships from going in and out of the Gulf of Oman, starting April 13, with a brief pause from June 18 to July 13. Anadolu via Getty Images - PHOTO: Commercial vessels and oil tankers sit anchored in the waters off Bandar Abbas in southern Iran's Hormozgan Province on Sept. 9, 2026. Attacks not isolated to ships crossing the strait Strikes have not been limited to ships. On Nov. 8, Iran attacked the Omani island of Didamar in the strait itself, according to satellite images and video verified by ABC News. The island hosts radar and satellite communications technology. Iranian state media said Iran had struck what it described as "enemy navigation aid systems." Oman, a U.S. partner, did not comment on the attack. Copernicus Sentinel 2 - PHOTO: Satellite image of Oman's Didamar island in the Strait of Hormuz following claimed Iranian attacks on infrastructure on the island. Strikes have also not been isolated to ships actively crossing the strait. ABC News has verified at least one incident in which a ship was attacked by a drone appearing to belong to Iran, despite not making any attempt to cross the strait. In early October, the Panama-flagged supertanker Gem No. 2 had been idle off the coast of the United Arab Emirates in the Persian Gulf, outside the Strait of Hormuz, for nearly five months. It was fully loaded with a cargo of two million barrels of Saudi crude oil, per maritime intelligence company Kpler, and was one of the hundreds of ships the International Maritime Organization estimates is stuck in the Persian Gulf since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran. What happened to Gem No. 2? Two crew members who were on board Gem No. 2 say the ship never attempted to cross the Strait of Hormuz, and that it was attacked by one drone on Oct. 9 and then at least three others on Oct. 10, the latter attack sparking a massive fire and forcing the ship's evacuation, according to videos filmed by the crew obtained and verified by ABC News. Obtained by ABC News - PHOTO: Oil Tanker Gem No2 on fire after being hit by drones while sitting idle off the coast of the United Arab Emirates in October 2026. Hours after the vessel was struck for a second time and evacuated, the Iranian Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said in an online post that the vessel had struck a naval mine while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz through an "unauthorized" route. Satellite images taken in the days after it was abandoned confirm Gem No. 2's position off the coast of the UAE, well outside the Strait of Hormuz. Copernicus Sentinel 2 - PHOTO: Satellite image of oil tanker Gem No2 off the coast of the UAE on October 24, two weeks after being attacked. ABC News showed images taken by the crew of the wreckage of the drone that struck the ship on Oct. 9 to Fabian Hinz, a researcher who studies drone warfare. Hinz said the wreckage in the images belongs to a jet-powered Hadid-110, built by Iran. Iran continues to say the ship hit a mine. Large tankers targeted: Analyst Azizi, the ICG's Iran analyst, suggested that "large oil tankers seem to be receiving particular attention, whether they are moving through the strait or operating elsewhere in the Persian Gulf." "One possible explanation is that Tehran wants to discourage the use of supertankers and prevent the development of alternative shipping arrangements that could make the blockade less effective," he said. Obtained by ABC News - PHOTO: Pieces of a drone that hit oil tanker Gem No2 on October 9th, identified as an Iranian Hadid-110 drone by an expert to ABC News. It's not clear why Gem No. 2 was allegedly targeted, but the vessel would have been an easy target, according to Samir Madani, co-founder of TankerTrackers.c o m . Madani told ABC News he noticed Gem No. 2 before the attack because the tanker's location transmission services were turned on, revealing its location publicly. Both Azizi and Toossi describe Iran's actions in the Strait of Hormuz as having "strategic logic." "Ultimately, the objective goes beyond disrupting oil exports. Iran is trying to demonstrate that the United States cannot guarantee maritime security in the Persian Gulf despite its overwhelming naval superiority," Azizi told ABC News. Toossi added that this strategy will have consequences far beyond the strait. "The danger is that this escalating contest will produce a much wider disruption of regional shipping and energy infrastructure, with even greater consequences for the global economy," he said. articles.title: GOP set to block Trump Pentagon picks as other military moves face headwinds
articles.summary: Senate Republicans are poised to block at least two of President Donald Trump’s nominees for senior Pentagon roles, escalating intense policy disagreements within the GOP, according to current and former officials familiar with the matter. Austin Dahmer and Alex Velez-Green were nominated more than a year ago to become the Pentagon policy office’s director of strategy, plans and capabilities and as the office’s deputy director, respectively. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. But despite months of lobbying by the administration, neither has enough votes to advance, and they will not be among a final batch of nominees considered by the Senate this year, those familiar with the matter said. Like others, these people spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss the situation. A spokesperson for the Senate Armed Services Committee’s Republican majority did not respond to a request for comment. Democrats, who will take control of Congress in January following their blowout victory in the midterm elections, are not expected to support Dahmer and Velez-Green either, the current and former officials said. With six weeks to go before Republicans lose their majorities on Capitol Hill, the stalled nominations are one of several areas where the Trump administration is encountering obstacles to its priorities for the Pentagon, including its plans for a $1.5 trillion defense budget. The White House is also running out of time to secure Senate confirmation of its picks for Navy secretary and the Army’s top officer. A senior Pentagon official said in an interview that it was possible Dahmer and Velez-Green may be renominated for the same positions next year and that the Defense Department wasn’t ruling out the potential for them to advance in a Democratic-controlled Senate. A White House spokesperson, Olivia Wales, called on Congress to confirm Trump’s nominees “without delay,” but declined to address specific questions for this report. Top Pentagon officials have urged Republicans to use their remaining time in power to pass $350 billion in defense funding through a party-line process that would not require any Democratic support. The money would pay for a range of military equipment, some of which would help the Pentagon recover from the strain on munitions and weapons platforms caused by the administration’s war with Iran. Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg visited Capitol Hill on Wednesday to lobby Republicans on the effort. In a sign that the GOP does not consider such a large sum realistic, Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota) told reporters afterward that he would first attempt to pass a bipartisan defense spending bill with Democrats. Dahmer and Velez-Green previously served as national security advisers in the Senate. While awaiting confirmation, they have held acting roles as senior deputies to Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby. Velez-Green has helped lead the Pentagon’s review of U.S. military posture in Europe, while Dahmer has helped write high-level strategy documents. Resistance to their nominations began last year amid what has become an acrimonious feud between Colby and congressional Republicans that has come to represent a broader debate within the Republican Party over Trump’s “America First” foreign policy. A year ago, shortly before their confirmation hearings, the Pentagon announced it was withdrawing an Army brigade from Romania despite the objections of GOP defense hawks, who publicly criticized both officials for failing to consult lawmakers before finalizing the decision. As The Washington Post reported in June, House Armed Services Committee Chair Mike Rogers (R-Alabama) later accused Colby of lying to him about the withdrawal - an allegation Colby has denied. The stalled confirmations have frustrated officials within the Pentagon exasperated by their inability to reach a deal with Senate Republicans, current and former officials said. At different points this year, staff within the Pentagon policy office suggested that officials from the Baltic nations that border Russia opposed the two nominees and were, in part, responsible for the impasse, according to one current and one former official - who said the allegation was false. The senior Pentagon official said that the administration had heard from multiple sources that Baltic officials had spoken poorly of Dahmer and Velez-Green but that it was unclear how influential those comments were. They also said the Defense Department does not blame the countries for the Senate’s decision to block the nominations. Spokespeople for the Latvian, Lithuanian and Estonian embassies in Washington either did not respond to or declined requests for comment. The Pentagon has instead prioritized the confirmation of other Trump nominees, including Hung Cao, tapped to lead the Navy, and Gen. Chris LaNeve, the administration’s pick for Army chief of staff. Cao encountered bipartisan frustration during his Senate confirmation hearing this week, as lawmakers vented about the Trump administration’s responsiveness to Congress and its desire to replace the electromagnetic catapults that launch fighters from aircraft carriers with older steam-powered systems - a change that could cost billions of dollars. “Returning to steam is a nonstarter and everybody needs to understand that,” Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Mississippi), the Senate Armed Services Committee chair, told Cao during the hearing. Because he only recently retired from the Navy, Cao will require a 60-vote waiver in the Senate to be confirmed as the service’s next civilian leader. Multiple Democrats on the committee said after the hearing that they will oppose his confirmation. Trump appointed Cao the Navy’s acting secretary after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pushed out Cao’s predecessor, billionaire John Phelan, in April. LaNeve, the Army’s vice chief of staff, was made the service’s acting military leader after Hegseth fired the job’s former occupant, Gen. Randy George. Hegseth has declined to explain why he fired George, despite facing questions from Republicans and Democrats supportive of the ousted general. As The Post reported in August, LaNeve urged George shortly before his firing to drop an internal investigation into whether Army helicopter pilots broke regulations by flying past country musician Kid Rock’s Nashville home. Hegseth later ended the investigation himself, posting a message on social media in support of the soldiers involved in the flyby. Some Republicans have privately opposed LaNeve’s nomination, which has been delayed for months despite Hegseth urging the White House to formally tap him for the role, current and former officials said. Trump did so Tuesday. Sen. Joni Ernst (Iowa), a retiring Republican who has opposed LaNeve’s confirmation, said that she would “love to see this work out” but that a successful outcome was “probably up to the administration.” The Army has no Senate-confirmed service secretary either. The job is currently held on an acting basis by Adam Telle. His predecessor, Dan Driscoll, resigned after repeated clashes with Hegseth. The Trump administration has not yet announced its nominee to permanently lead the service. articles.title: Anthropic engineer proposes a theory for all these outages
articles.summary: There have been so many prominent tech services experiencing outages lately that the problems have gone mainstream in a new way we haven't seen before. Besides the headlines and podcasts (some of which are asking if this is actually a new thing or if we're just noticing it more), the tech outages have kept Vice President JD Vance from attending New York events , led to the resignation of the White House's cybersecurity chief , made “Saturday Night Live,” and been the subject of tons of memes and TikTok comedy where people joke that "LinkedIn and Tinder must be down, because I'm not getting any responses!" As we wrote recently , the problems are far more than just cybersecurity, though AI means hackers can discover and exploit bugs like never before. Infrastructure is decrepit. Maintenance is deferred. Exhausted, too-small teams of IT workers aren't up to this level of chaos. But there's another explanation that's perhaps underappreciated: one big downside of Claude Code, the marquee product that has given Anthropic ( ANT ) its trillion-dollar valuation. The problem is best explained by someone who would know best: a prominent Anthropic engineer (and former Google engineer) who works on Claude Code as a member of the technical staff, Addy Osmani, whose treatise on " comprehension debt " bounced around the software engineering community in March — and is even more relevant today. What Osmani highlights isn't really a weakness in Claude Code, but in how companies and engineering teams use it. The gist: AI can write code faster than we can review it. The speed is a great benefit, but it's also a curse, as myriad companies pivot from writing code to overseeing teams of AI agents that complain less and write more. As Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said this week , the company's engineers  "build a software factory that builds the product. They don't build the product." Dario Amodei is seen on the display at the Nasdaq MarketSite as shares of Anthropic begin trading after their IPO in Times Square, New York City, United States, on Nov. 19, 2026. (Stephanie Keith/NurPhoto via Getty Images) NurPhoto via Getty Images Traditionally, the laborious process of checking other people's code is how software engineers internalize why systems are designed the way they are, and why decisions from earlier in a project might be meaningful today. But reviewing the entirety of AI code isn't feasible given how fast we can produce it now. It's too unwieldy, and this represents a massive bottleneck for progress. Tests, AI review, and spending less time reviewing can be effective. But they've removed layers of verification, and ultimately comprehension, which is disappearing, Osmani explains. All this means that with code piling up faster than humans can review it, companies can lose control of their systems in a way far more prosaic and banal than some sort of sentient AI or Skynet doomsday scenario. With human code proofreaders at their limits, when things inevitably break , that missing understanding matters. Coders — or even AI — may not realize that a few lines of code represent an important piece of figurative duct tape, a load-bearing wall, or a mechanism that triggers other contingencies. Every patch or attempted fix can also break more things. That brings us back to the wave of cyber outages . Aside from a few high-profile lawsuits and public scandals, the tech giants whose software "ate the world" and that now commandeer our attention spans have largely escaped meaningful accountability. Their software failures are embarrassing. And their design choices have led to allegations of addiction, anti-social behavior, and economic exploitation. But they have, generally speaking, escaped rigorous regulation. AI changes the calculus. The era of honor system self-policing may be coming to an end. "When AI-generated code is running in healthcare systems, financial infrastructure, and government services," Osmani wrote, the excuse that an AI wrote bad code and we didn't fully review it "will not hold up in a post-incident report when lives or significant assets are at stake." Cyber outages are often a nuisance and, mercifully, haven't led to a mass-casualty event or prolonged economic crisis. But in a world where AI can generate code faster than anyone can keep up, it's not hard to imagine that changing. articles.title: Zelensky calls Putin a 'killer' after Trump describes him as a friend
articles.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Vladimir Putin is a "killer" in response to Donald Trump referring to the Russian leader as his "friend" in China this week. Speaking to CNN, Zelensky said it was up to the US president "how to call Putin" but "for us, he is an enemy... for us, he's a killer". Before Thursday's historic trilateral meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Putin, Trump called Putin his "friend" and said the two leaders have had a "great relationship for many years". Russian attacks continued overnight, with two people killed, including a boy, and 52 injured in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region, officials said. Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west. On Friday, at least nine people were killed in Russian strikes targeting bridges in the capital Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine - with Zelensky calling the attack the "biggest this year" after an onslaught of 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic, and more than 400 drones. The strikes came days after Ukraine had badly damaged the Crimean Bridge. [EPA] Hours after Friday's strikes on Ukraine, Trump told reporters at the White House that Putin would "love to end the war". "They [Zelensky and Putin] both want to end it and it's a very good thing I have a relationship," he said on Friday. Trump also doubled down on his description of the Russian leader as a friend but said he "can't speak" to whether Putin is a friend to the US. However Zelensky said despite Trump's stance, he saw Putin as "a killer". "I think mostly for the people in the world, he is a killer because he's killing - by the way- he's killing each day and night," he told CNN. Zelensky also said speaking about Putin like he was a "friend" meant "he doesn't feel enough pressure". The war of words came as neighbouring Poland said a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace in the south-east of the country early on Friday. Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said the missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border. This was about 100km from where European troops - from 11 of the 36 member nations of the coalition of the willing - were completing a training exercise, Polish authorities said.  Another cruise missile and a jet-powered drone were suspected to have hit two other locations, they added. On Saturday, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told the BBC the cruise missiles had guidance systems, so "it is very unlikely that they veered off course as a result of Ukrainian electronic warfare". "This is a war in Europe that affects our security," he told Radio 4's Today programme, also referencing similar incidents in recent months across Europe. Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said the military alliance had scrambled its jets in response. Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during Friday's massive attack on Ukraine. Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. articles.title: DOJ turns attention to Democratic operatives in Alaska Senate election probe
articles.summary: Alaska Democratic Senator-elect Mary Peltola looks on during a midterm election night watch party in Anchorage, Alaska, on November 3. - Justin Sullivan/Getty Images/File With Alaska’s Senate race now called, the Justice Department is shifting focus toward Sen.-elect Mary Peltola’s campaign as part of its ongoing criminal investigation into an alleged scheme to run a spoiler candidate against her opponent, according to two people familiar with the matter. The focus marks a shift in the investigation, which thrust the Justice Department into the center of a contentious political race. For months, investigators had focused on whether former candidate Daniel J. Sullivan intended to siphon votes from Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, whose name is similar. Just before the election, however, a New York Times report described an alleged coordinated effort involving the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) to improve her chances of victory. Peltola has publicly said she was not aware of the alleged effort. With public pressure from President Donald Trump and from Justice Department headquarters, some officials weighed whether a possible charge could be brought against the alleged spoiler candidate nicknamed “Decoy Dan,” according to one of the people familiar with the discussions. The investigation has since shifted away from Daniel J. Sullivan and is now focused on Peltola’s campaign, the DSCC and outside political consultants allegedly involved in the scheme, another person familiar with the matter said. The Justice Department also has sent dozens of FBI agents to Alaska and issued hundreds of subpoenas and preservation letters as part of the probe, that person said. Gerald Heikes , a longshot candidate, was issued a subpoena as part of a DOJ probe, CNN previously reported. More than a dozen people have received letters saying they may be targets of the investigation, CNN has reported. Democrats have denounced the investigation as politically motivated, arguing that recruiting spoiler candidates is a common and legal strategy. Meanwhile, the Justice Department has moved to drop its lawsuit seeking to block certification of Peltola’s victory. The suit argued that certification should be delayed while an investigation determined whether voters had been confused. A judge rejected the Justice Department’s longshot certification delay effort before Election Day, a move that hinged on whether the margin of Peltola’s victory was larger than the number of votes Daniel J. Sullivan received. The official count shows that even if Daniel J. Sullivan’s votes were counted for Sen. Sullivan, Peltola would still win. Two days after the race was decided, the administration asked a court to declare the case moot. CNN has reached out to the Peltola campaign and the DSCC for comment. articles.summary: 今年，美国投资级（IG）债券发行已创历史纪录，发行量达到1.88万亿美元。而明年IG债券总供应量预计将进一步攀升至2.1万亿美元。 然而，2027年存量债券到期规模约1万亿美元，叠加利率中枢上移推动年度票息收入升至5560亿美元，扣除到期与票息回流后的“净净”供给约5080亿美元，仍低于2020年峰值；净发行量1.06万亿美元仅占市场规模的11.2%，与11.0%的长期历史均值基本持平。高额到期与票息回流形成有效对冲，使总供给虽再创纪录，净吸收压力并未同步极端化。 供给结构明显向科技倾斜：预计2027年科技与媒体合计发行6120亿美元，约占全市场净发行量50%；其中AI相关融资约4500亿美元、同比增长64%，超大规模企业2250亿美元，数据中心与GPU融资合计2250亿美元。 AI资本开支由数据中心基建向芯片算力采购切换，融资期限显著缩短，超大规模科技公司正从长端向短端迁移。今年长端集中发行一度推陡信用利差曲线；但并购融资预计同比下滑52%至1440亿美元，期限多在5-7年的GPU融资将成为下一阶段主力，2027年IG发行将明显向前端与中段倾斜。 天量供给叠加 4.1万亿美元表外杠杆急剧膨胀 ，使AI融资成为悬在信用市场上空的房间里的大象。美联储鹰派立场推高实际收益率，但IG利差并未广泛走阔：JULI利差维持在100bp附近，BofA指数利差处于历史偏紧区间，收益率约6.26%，显示投资者仍具备吸收供给的能力；一级市场巨额发行主要靠IG公募基金与ETF创纪录流入、以及资金状况改善的企业养老金买盘承接。 2.1万亿美元总供给的表面压力能否超过净吸收能力，将决定美国信用市场是延续总量有韧性、结构分化的格局，还是走向更广泛的利差重定价。

articles.title: 郭明錤：谷歌将明年博通设计TPU出货量下调20%，计划增加联发科份额
articles.summary: 谷歌正在调整人工智能芯片采购策略，削减博通设计的高端TPU订单，同时计划增加联发科设计芯片的采购量。在数据中心电力供应和芯片产能双重受限的背景下，谷歌正重新分配算力资源。 据知名苹果及供应链分析师郭明錤最新行业调查， 谷歌已将博通设计的TPU 8i系列2027年出货量削减约100万颗，降幅约占该系列全年出货量的20%，其中定价较高的8i Max（代号Whalefish）受影响最大。 与此同时，谷歌计划提高联发科设计的TPU 8t系列出货量，但具体规模尚未确定。 这一调整可能给博通带来压力。作为谷歌TPU的核心设计合作伙伴，高端型号订单缩减或影响其定制芯片业务收入；联发科则有望借此扩大在谷歌AI基础设施供应链中的份额。 前沿模型优先，算力分配逻辑生变 郭明錤指出，谷歌近几个月多次强调，前沿模型开发将优先获得算力资源。此次调整TPU 8i与8t的采购组合，正是这一策略在供应链产能紧张和数据中心电力受限背景下的体现。 在资源约束下，谷歌倾向于将有限的高端算力集中用于前沿模型研发，而非继续扩大高价芯片的部署规模。 8i Max订单削减尤为明显，也反映出谷歌对芯片成本与算力资源配置的重新权衡。 与此同时，提高TPU 8t系列采购量，意味着谷歌希望通过调整芯片组合，在资源受限的情况下维持算力部署。联发科设计的8t系列最终增量仍未敲定，实际出货规模有待进一步观察。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 俄乌和平谈判重启，结束冲突的前景再度受到关注。 据媒体近日报道， 特朗普政府已向欧洲和乌克兰官员传达，希望基辅在明年1月初之前与俄罗斯达成和平协议，并通过近期一系列接触释放出强烈的时间紧迫感。 这一时间表令基辅担忧，乌克兰总统泽连斯基可能被迫接受一份以莫斯科条件为基础的协议。 据 新华社11月12日报道 ，俄罗斯总统普京当天在莫斯科会见美国总统特使威特科夫和特朗普女婿库什纳时表示，对俄方来说，任何外国军队在乌克兰驻扎都绝对不可接受，这会威胁俄安全，乌境内的外国军队是俄合法打击目标。威特科夫希望此次与普京会面能促成新一轮有欧洲方面代表参与的多方会谈。 特使威特科夫与库什纳本月在阿布扎比重启俄乌谈判，结束因中东冲突中断八个月的接触。此后，两人又先后前往莫斯科、都柏林和柏林，与俄乌及欧洲官员密集会晤。特朗普在与普京会面后称，后者已明确表示莫斯科“准备好实现和平”。 美方施压的影响已开始显现。乌克兰官员将Starshield（SpaceX星链的军用版本）近期受到的速率限制，以及“爱国者”拦截导弹交付延迟数月，视为美国削弱基辅谈判地位、迫使其让步的信号。 时间表背后的政治算术 推动这一时间表的核心是美国国内政治。 特朗普所属的共和党在本月中期选举中同时失去众议院和参议院控制权，民主党预计将加强对乌支持，并推动对俄罗斯采取更强硬措施。据报道援引四位知情人士，白宫因此希望在民主党接管国会前敲定协议。 尽管特朗普在和平谈判方面仍拥有广泛权力，民主党人仍可利用立法权增加对乌援助、推动对俄制裁，并通过国会监督调查特朗普的外交政策，以及威特科夫和库什纳的商业利益。 基辅对此尤为担忧。 据报道援引一位乌克兰高级官员，特朗普“喜欢普京，想在一月前把这一切了结”，并警告称，如果协议在这一期限前达成，俄罗斯“可能获得更好的条件”。 欧洲官员也表达了类似忧虑。 美方急、俄方不急 谈判双方的节奏明显不对称。据报道，一位欧洲官员在会见威特科夫和库什纳后表示： “美国人在使劲推，也有人担心，要接近达成协议需要乌克兰作出大量让步。” 另一位欧洲官员则直言： “美国人很着急，普京一点也不急。” 俄罗斯的核心要求并未松动。普京周四与特朗普会晤后表示，乌克兰及其欧洲盟友必须接受“妥协”和“现实”。俄方要求基辅交出顿巴斯前线关键地区，放弃加入北约，并限制乌克兰武装力量；同时要求北约从东翼撤回部队和武器部署，调整欧洲冷战后的安全秩序。 莫斯科也没有快速达成协议的明显动力。报道援引两位了解克里姆林宫思路的人士称，俄方计划继续通过空袭增加谈判筹码。此外，普京坚持将欧洲更广泛的安全问题纳入最终协议，而相关议题才刚开始进入谈判。 这意味着，除非乌克兰及其欧洲盟友作出重大让步，否则俄方接受美方推动的快速协议并不容易。 安全保障：一个尚未落地的构想 美方提出，可由西方国家参照北约第五条款的集体防御模式，为乌克兰提供安全保障。库什纳周四在柏林表示，他认为特朗普愿意接受这一方案，并称美方已让俄罗斯接受安全保障以第五条款为基础的概念。 但特朗普本人对此仍未给出明确承诺。周五被问及是否可能向乌克兰提供此类保障、是否与普京讨论过时， 他表示：“我们这边会发布一些东西，因为这也是一场公关战。”“我们会说一些话，他们也会说一些话。” 俄方则迅速表明反对立场。参加阿布扎比最新一轮谈判的俄罗斯副外长Sergei Ryabkov周五通过国际文传电讯社表示，即便是对基辅而言相当于准北约成员身份的安排，俄罗斯也无法接受。 他强调，乌克兰必须承诺永远不加入北约，只有这一要求得到满足，俄方才愿意讨论安全保障问题。 欧洲的席位与G20的悬念 欧洲国家主张先实现停火，再讨论更广泛的安全框架，并要求在谈判中获得正式席位。 俄罗斯虽承认欧洲需要参与最终协议，但普京尚未承诺扩大谈判范围，表示要等欧洲官员与俄方在莫斯科会晤后再作决定。 据报道援引两位官员透露，美国官员还提出，特朗普可能在下月于迈阿密举行的G20峰会上，与欧洲领导人讨论结束战争的方案。但一位法国高级官员表示，峰会期间不会就乌克兰问题与欧洲方面举行谈判，因为乌克兰并未受邀。 特朗普已邀请普京出席峰会，但这位俄罗斯领导人尚未表态是否参加。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 恒生科技指数迎史上最大调整：30只扩至50只，近300亿港元资金待配置
articles.summary: 11月20日，恒生指数公司发布今年第三季度恒生指数系列季度检讨结果。恒生指数、恒生国企指数、恒生科技指数及恒生综合指数的成份股变动将于2026年12月4日收市后实施，并于2026年12月7日起生效。 恒生指数成份股没有变动，成份股数目维持95只。恒生国企指数成份股数目维持50只，纳入智谱、MINIMAX-W，剔除邮储银行、申洲国际。 恒生科技指数成份股由30只扩容至50只，纳入建滔集团、瑞声科技、立讯精密、胜宏科技、禾赛-W、英诺赛科、中际旭创、迅策、宁德时代、金山云、壁仞科技、澜起科技、长飞光纤光缆、优必选等。 对此，业内人士认为，本次恒生科技指数成份股由30只一次性扩容至50只，新增名单覆盖先进硬件、光通信、算力、半导体、智能驾驶、机器人等赛道，或意味着恒生科技指数底层定位切换。 一名港股市场资深人士对记者表示，恒生科技指数已从“互联网平台指数”转向“泛硬科技指数”。“过去恒生科技指数可选消费行业占比较高，缺乏AI、算力、芯片股。新纳入股票以先进硬件、人工智能主题为主，这些调整有望进一步呈现当前港股科技产业全貌。”上述人士表示。 10月7日，恒生指数公司公布恒生科技指数编算方法修订方案的市场咨询总结。恒生指数公司表示，将从扩大科技主题覆盖、引入分组选股机制两方面修订指数。业内人士表示，这是恒生科技指数2020年发布以来最大的一次修订。 在扩大科技主题覆盖方面，恒生指数公司表示，将采纳早前提出的修订方案，取消合资格候选公司必须属于恒生行业分类系统五个指定行业的要求。 在采纳此前修订方案的基础上，恒生指数公司对恒生科技指数主题进行了整合与拓展，并新增了前沿科技主题。调整后的六大科技主题包括：数字平台与解决方案、人工智能、先进硬件、机器人及自动化、云计算以及前沿科技。同时，恒生科技指数的科技子主题由16个增至24个。 在选股机制上，恒生科技指数引入了分组选股机制。恒生指数公司采纳早前提出的修订方案，将选股范畴由主板上市公司修订至恒生综合大中型股指数成份股，并正式引入双组别选股机制。新机制分别以市值排名和收入增长排名作为选股准则，其中非现有成份股须满足过去三个月日均成交额不低于1亿港元的条件，按收入增长排名入选的个股则须在最近连续两个财政年度均实现至少5亿港元的年收入，从流动性和基本面两个维度设定了明确的准入门槛。 恒生科技指数50只成份股中，前40只按市值排名选取，侧重覆盖大市值龙头；剩余10只按过去12个月的收入增长排名选取，为具备高成长潜力的科技企业提供纳入空间。这一调整在扩大指数代表性的同时，也强化了科技主题投资的成长属性。 中信证券发布研报认为，恒生科技指数编算方案的修订主要由港股科技板块结构性变化引起。港股科技板块早期高度集中于互联网业务，近年来先进硬件与人工智能相关上市公司的数量显著增加，特专科技公司也陆续登陆市场。 “同时，港股科技板块收入增长较强的公司往往市值较小，在仅以公司市值为基础的选股框架下，高增长但规模相对较小的公司或未能被纳入指数。此次恒生科技指数编算方案修订的核心要义，在于使其成为更广泛、更具前瞻性的港股科技股基准指数。”中信证券认为。 此次修订对市场最直接的影响，是被动资金的大规模重新配置。 恒生指数公司数据显示，截至2026年9月底，被动式追踪恒生指数系列的产品资产管理总值约为1055亿美元，其中追踪恒生科技指数的资产管理规模已从2020年推出初期的15亿美元，增长至371亿美元。今年10月，广发证券发布研报表示，恒生科技指数新增成份股对应的配置需求约为291亿港元。 本文来源： 上海证券报 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “脱欧”十年之后，英国又要“入欧”？
articles.summary: 脱欧十年之后，英国正站在是否重返欧盟的门槛上。首相伯纳姆‌本周五在布鲁塞尔公布一揽子协议，并明确提出英国应就是否回归这一重要贸易集团展开辩论——这让“脱欧、悔脱欧、再入欧”的政治链条第一次有了现实轮廓。 据《华尔街日报》近日报道，伯纳姆‌与欧盟方面达成的“重置”协议包括取消大部分食品和农产品边境检查、重启学生交流项目。 欧盟委员会主席Ursula von der Leyen称，这标志着英欧关系的“转折点”。伯纳姆‌则称，这是一份“双赢”协议，是“英国的好日子，也是欧洲的好日子”。 但协议落地仍存变数。 欧洲谈判代表明确表示，除非欧盟学生在英国大学能享受更低学费，否则协议不会全面执行，双方同意在未来六个月继续谈判。 伯纳姆‌也承认，这“很可能已是本届议会任期内能够达成的上限”。 对市场而言，信号意义大于短期经济效果。伯纳姆‌称，协议最多可为英国经济带来相当于GDP 0.5%的增量；高盛研究则显示，若英国重返欧盟单一市场，经济总量可能提升2%至5%。但重入进程漫长、成本不确定，英国可能由此面临持续数年的政治不确定性。 十年之后，民意天平倒向“回归” 2016年公投中，52%的英国选民选择脱欧，四年后英国正式退出欧盟。如今，多项民调平均显示，62%的英国人希望重返欧盟，38%希望留在欧盟之外。 伯纳姆‌本周直言：“我们得到的脱欧方案没有奏效。我们失去的比得到的多。” 这与前任斯塔默的谨慎路线形成对比。斯塔默于2024年带领工党重新执政后，主张“让脱欧运转起来”，通过有限协议和部分监管对齐降低贸易摩擦，但未能扭转政策方向。伯纳姆‌接任后，仅用四个月便在欧洲议题上展现出更鲜明的立场。 上月，伯纳姆‌表示希望在有生之年看到英国重返欧盟，但排除在本届议会任期内推动，同时突破工党2024年竞选纲领中不重返单一市场、不重返关税同盟、不恢复人员自由流动的“红线”。 他承诺在本次峰会后，启动与欧盟关于长期关系选项的讨论。 协议内容有限，症结仍在学费与规则让渡 本次峰会达成的成果具体而有限。据CNN报道，协议涵盖青年交流计划、碳排放交易体系对接以及削减食品贸易壁垒。其中，青年计划允许英欧各10万名年轻人在对方境内最多居留三年，用于工作、学习或旅行，预计不迟于2030年1月落地。 但协议全面实施仍受学费问题制约。据《华尔街日报》报道，欧盟谈判代表要求欧洲学生在英国大学享受与英国学生相近的低学费待遇。双方周五发布的联合声明称，将就此达成补充协议，预计在未来六个月内完成谈判。 规则让渡同样是争议焦点。 英国欧洲事务大臣Hamish Falconer向BBC承认，协议实施意味着英国必须接受欧盟产品监管规则，却无权参与制定。这正是脱欧辩论中长期存在的矛盾：英国希望减少贸易壁垒，却不愿放弃监管自主权。 重入路径多选项，但每一条都有代价 英国可能的重返路径主要有三种，各自对应不同程度的市场准入与主权让渡。 其一是加入关税同盟 ，实行统一对外关税、便利双边商品贸易，同时保留服务业监管自主权，但英国商品进入欧盟单一市场仍可能面临部分检查。 其二是参照挪威模式加入单一市场 ，接受欧盟规则、允许人员自由流动并缴纳相关费用，但无权参与规则制定。 其三是全面重返欧盟 ，承担更高会费并恢复人员自由流动，同时重新获得参与贸易集团决策的权利。 但英国未必能获得当年享有的特殊条件。报道指出，保留本币、享受会费折扣等原有优势都没有保证，而一旦这些条件无法延续，公众对重返欧盟的支持可能减弱。 智库“英国与变化的欧洲”负责人Anand Menon表示：“没有按钮能让你回到2016年。”他警告，重返议题可能长期占据政治议程，增加经济不确定性，并分散政府处理国内问题的精力。 “认为当初离开是个坏主意，并不等于认为现在应该加入。” 欧盟方面也并不急于推动。欧盟外交与安全政策高级代表Kaja Kallas上周表示，英国脱欧给欧盟造成了“大量创伤”，未来谈判“不会那么容易”。Carnegie Europe主任Rosa Balfour则指出，英国重返并非欧盟的首要议题，欧盟希望确认英国提出的新关系方案能够长期维持。von der Leyen虽然表示愿与英国就未来关系展开讨论，但也没有承诺具体时间表。 反对声浪重启，经济时机却略显尴尬 英国国内的反对力量正在重新集结。据《华尔街日报》报道，名为“Stay Out”的阵营已在社交媒体上大量投放内容。前首相鲍里斯·约翰逊称，伯纳姆‌会因此“把自己和工党钉死”；发起脱欧公投的前首相卡梅伦则呼吁政府优先处理税收、债务、住房和国防等国内问题。 保守党领袖Kemi Badenoch指责伯纳姆‌没有吸取过去的教训，改革党领袖Nigel Farage则称他没有获得与布鲁塞尔推动更紧密关系的授权。 YouGov调查显示，重返欧盟在选民优先事项中仅排第九，远低于经济、移民和医疗。 经济环境也让重返欧盟面临新的权衡。多数经济学家认为脱欧损害了英国经济，但也指出英国并未借此推进去监管和提升竞争力。与此同时，据《华尔街日报》报道， 英国近几个季度经济表现好于预期，部分得益于更快的AI应用。一些人士担心，欧盟更严格的AI监管可能限制这一增长动力。 民意支持与实际政策选择之间仍存在距离。民调研究机构Persuasion UK副主任Morgan Jones认为，如果英国明天就能按照2016年的条件重返欧盟，这一选项将获得压倒性支持，对工党争取不同群体选民也有吸引力。但她指出，预算分摊、加入欧元区的风险以及漫长的谈判过程，都可能让选民逐渐失去耐心。 articles.title: 国内反对、海外也不行？特朗普威胁对“海外建设数据中心”加重税
articles.summary: 美国AI基础设施投资面临新的政策与现实阻力，企业全球算力布局的不确定性进一步上升。 11月21日，据媒体报道，特朗普周五在白宫新闻发布室对记者表示： “我们不会允许我们的公司在美国以外建设数据中心。” 他称，美国此前允许企业在芯片等领域向海外转移产能，对美国造成了严重损害，因此不会允许类似情况在数据中心领域重演。 特朗普还表示， 美国将对试图在海外建设数据中心的企业征收“巨额税费”或施加其他惩罚。不过，他没有说明禁令将通过何种方式实施，也承认尚未与政府团队讨论这一计划：“我甚至还没跟我的人说过这件事。” 这一表态也凸显出美国AI基础设施建设面临的另一重矛盾：特朗普希望推动数据中心在美国扩张，但相关项目在美国国内正遭遇越来越多的社区反对。电力消耗、基础设施压力等问题，已经成为美国数据中心扩张面临的现实阻力。 政策细节尚不明确，国内数据中心建设也面临阻力 据报道，目前尚不清楚特朗普具体设想采取何种措施，以及如何落实这一禁令。白宫方面也未立即回应置评请求。 对美国科技企业而言，海外数据中心是全球算力布局的重要组成部分。土地、电力供应和建设成本等因素都会影响项目选址。 如果海外建设受到限制，企业可能需要重新调整投资计划，在美国本土寻找更多建设资源，也可能面临更高的基础设施成本。 与此同时，美国国内对数据中心扩张的反对声音持续上升。据媒体报道， 在今年的中期选举中，数据中心成为选民关注的重要议题，承诺限制数据中心扩张的候选人获得了明显支持。 随着相关项目增加，电力消耗、当地基础设施负担及社区影响引发越来越多争议。 特朗普此前多次反对州和地方政府限制数据中心建设，认为数据中心能够带来就业、税收和经济增长。 今年8月，他曾呼吁社区不要叫停相关项目，周五再次表示，应当让数据中心为当地社区创造收益，而不是将其关停。 AI交易承压，算力投资再添政策不确定性 特朗普的最新表态为AI产业带来新的政策风险。美国科技企业一方面需要持续扩大算力规模，另一方面可能面临海外建设受限、本土项目又遭遇地方阻力的双重约束。若相关限制落地，企业的全球数据中心选址和资本开支安排都可能受到影响。 这一政策风险出现之际，AI交易本身已显露疲态。标普500指数自11月4日以来累计下跌约9%，投资者对AI股票估值及投资回报的担忧持续升温。 即便Anthropic本周完成创纪录规模的IPO，也未能缓解市场对AI股票估值可持续性的忧虑。 特朗普此前曾对Anthropic及其Claude聊天机器人表示赞赏，但对AI产业的支持也伴随着对企业投资地点的限制要求。对于正大举投入数据中心建设的美国科技企业而言，海外布局与本土扩张都可能面临新的政策和现实约束。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “文娱史上最成功发售，堪比007、星球大战、米老鼠”！GTA 6发行首日收入高达38亿美元
articles.summary: 《GTA 6》以创纪录的首日收入，成为文娱史上最成功的发行项目之一。 11月21日，据彭博，Take-Two Interactive旗下 Rockstar Games新作《Grand Theft Auto VI》（简称《GTA 6》）发售首日全球收入达到37.9亿美元 ，超过《复仇者联盟4：终局之战》约29亿美元的全球票房，也高于Taylor Swift“Eras”巡演约20亿美元的销售额。 美国银行分析师认为，《GTA》已成为与007、星球大战和米老鼠比肩的跨代际IP。 数据显示，《GTA 6》预售销量达到3250万份，创下游戏发行纪录。Sensor Tower数据显示，超过80%的预购玩家选择售价100美元的Ultimate Edition，而非80美元的标准版。 游戏发售首日还在直播平台掀起热潮。据CNN报道，玩家在Twitch、YouTube和Kick上的累计观看时长超过1.32亿小时，刷新直播平台纪录。 Take-Two股价周五盘中一度下跌，随后逆转收涨近1%，在科技股整体重挫的背景下跑赢大盘。 13年等待，首日收入达到前作4.7倍 《GTA 6》于11月19日正式发售，距离上一部正统续作《Grand Theft Auto V》已经过去13年。Rockstar为新作投入超过八年开发时间，目前拥有逾4700名员工。游戏以虚构的迈阿密“Vice City”为背景，围绕Jason和Lucia两名主角展开。 作为对比，《GTA 5》于2013年发售时，首个24小时销售额为8亿美元，三天内突破10亿美元。 《GTA 6》首日收入约为前作的4.7倍。据Sensor Tower数据，在正式发售前，该游戏已产生23.6亿美元收入，预售自6月开启，持续约五个月。 PC版与在线模式待推出，跨代际IP价值受关注 目前《GTA 6》尚未登陆PC平台。Take-Two表示，PC版本预计稍后推出，在线模式也在规划之中。这意味着PC端销售和线上业务的持续变现，仍有望成为后续收入来源。 美国银行全球研究部分析师Omar Dessouky指出， 此次发行推动《GTA》从一款电子游戏升级为与James Bond（007）、星球大战和米老鼠比肩的“跨代际IP”。更成熟的叙事有望重新吸引多年未接触游戏主机的玩家，而顶级画面与开放世界玩法则有助于吸引年轻用户。 Wedbush Securities分析师Alicia Reese表示，《GTA 6》为Rockstar构建更多游戏提供了新平台，未来数年都将令Take-Two受益。 发行热度也已延伸至游戏之外。Take-Two在迈阿密展开大规模营销，当地举办庆祝活动，NBA迈阿密热火的比赛也融入了游戏元素。Rockstar与PlayStation还计划在当地举办演唱会。随着感恩节假期到来，这款游戏有望继续推动假日季游戏消费。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
